findings.class: condition on the next stage (not a defect of the reviewed contracts)
findings.topic: no numeric tolerance band exists, so the item cannot emit a pass/fail judgement yet
findings.fact: limitPlan gives VAC2_PRST_Rise a DFT nominal of 4.15 V and VAC2_PRST_Hys a DFT nominal of 350 mV, both with toleranceStatus UNRESOLVED (lines 1186, 1205) and judgement PENDING_LIMIT_RULING; the DFT supplies no numeric bound (carried item TM109-OI-2 / MF-04).
findings.reviewerAssessment: the method contract handles this correctly: it computes, publishes and logs the values, marks them explicitly unjudged, and forbids inventing a tolerance from the Golden, from chip knowledge or from experience (limitPlan.rules). The contract is therefore compliant; the residual is a project-level decision, not a contract defect.
findings.conditionForImplementation: the implementation stage must reproduce the PENDING_LIMIT_RULING marker and must not synthesize a tolerance band; until a ruling arrives the item publishes measured values without a pass/fail verdict.
findings.neededToClose: one user ruling supplying the numeric minimum/maximum (or the tolerance) for VAC2_PRST_Rise and VAC2_PRST_Hys

findings.class: condition on the next stage (not a defect of the reviewed contracts)
findings.routedTo: test-strategy-architect (closing source: schematic-expert or a user ruling)
findings.topic: the signed boundary leaves two functional relay identities unresolved while both closures are empty
findings.fact: MF-01 and MF-02 are declared blocking=true by the method contract (openItems lines 1487-1506; handoff.blockingItems) and are relay-identity gaps owned by the strategy role: (a) the FR-001 default Cap2/stabiliser relay for the powered VBAT pin is not identified in the frozen DALI relay table (strategy C-04 / OI-S-02), and (b) the INT Toggle observation closure is empty, with the pad structure (open-drain versus push-pull) and any pull-up relay unasserted (RF-02). RG-1 and RG-3 are both the empty closure set in the signed contract.
findings.reviewerAssessment: this is not a method defect: the method contract registers both gaps, routes both to their owner, forbids the implementer from selecting a relay, and states that the electrical method itself is complete without them. It is a resource/relay ownership question, and per ROLE_ROUTING ('resource, route, relay and register issues return to strategy') it belongs to the strategy role, not to a method rework.
findings.conditionForImplementation: the implementation stage may code MP-1..MP-10 inside the signed boundary, but it must not select a relay: coding the empty RG-1/RG-3 closures as-is means the FR-001 Cap2 default closure is omitted and, if the INT pad is open-drain, the observed transition may not be present at all. The Captain must either have MF-01/MF-02 closed by the strategy owner first, or record explicitly that the implementation proceeds with empty RG-1/RG-3 closures and that the item's observability is then unproven.
findings.neededToClose: the frozen relay instance for the VBAT Cap2 closure (or an explicit waiver) and the INT pull-up instance plus the pad structure (or a ruling that the pad is push-pull)

limitations: This is a rule review of provenance, completeness and routing. It does not re-derive the DFT row or the schematic connectivity, so a wrong-but-well-located hardware fact inside the strategy contract would pass this gate; the strategy role's own conflicts and open items are the declared instrument for that risk.

The implementation-snapshot gate could not run at this stage because no implementation manifest exists; its substitute is the byte-exact frozen revision record, and the gate must be run for the IMPLEMENTATION review.
The two conditions RV-03 and RV-04 are forwarding obligations for the next stage; they do not change this verdict, which states only that the reviewed contracts are rule-complete and hash-frozen.
